Introduction

Northampton County Court is a city courthouse serving the residents of Pennsylvania. The appeals from the eastern district will go to the 3rd circuit United States court of appeals. The courthouse was established with a clerk's office in 1731 by John Marshall then a prison was established in this building in 1814. It has jurisdiction over the criminal, small claim, landlord-tenant, civil, family, juvenile, traffic, and vehicle matters. The court rules and procedures must be followed by every person that visits the court. Proper dressing is required in the courthouse. This courthouse consists of a magistrate court and common pleas court. An average of 70,000 cases were handled by the magistrate court each year.

Different courts of Northampton

How to search for case records?

Northampton County Court case search for records can be found online using https://pennsylvania.staterecords.org/northampton. The court maintains all the records online, in files, or a database. The case search can be done using the following ways:

  • Search by Case Number
  • Search by Traffic or Citation Number
  • Search by Name

After entering the data, the case information will come. This website will only show those records information that is publicly available. The sealed records are not available for the viewing of the public. Some records are unavailable; if the information does not come, the case records will be removed or confidential and cannot be displayed online. You have to mail a request form to https://www.pacourts.us/public-records/public-records-forms for these types of records. The court will decide whether to provide you with the information or not. You had to pay the mandatory fees for each per-page copy of the record if you need the records certified copies.

How to make a payment?

Northampton County Court payments can be made in the following ways:

· In-Person

A person can pay for tickets and fines by visiting the court during regular court hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the court payment window. Take your ticket and citation number with you when you come for payment. Service charges will be applied if you make a payment with a credit card.

· Online

Online payments can be made usinghttp://ujsportal.pacourts.us.Look up your case by using the name, case and citation number. After this, your case with the amount of the fine will be displayed. Pay using any online method. A convenience fee will be applied during this process.

· Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address; 669 Washington St, Easton, PA 18042, United States. Cash or personal checks are not acceptable in the mail; only certified checks or money orders are accepted. Remember to write your citation, name, case number, and account number when you send the payment, and mail the amount in a self-addressed, stamped envelope if you want a receipt.

Family law handles which types of cases?

Northampton County Court civil court handles cases related to family matters and they started handling these types of cases in 1978. The family matters include divorce, separation, child custody, support and visitation matters as well as juvenile matters. Co-parenting education programs are provided by this court in which the parents that filed for divorce learn some time management and different skills that can help in child custody and visitation matters. This program aims to reduce the impact of divorce on children and advise parents to give proper attention to their child’s needs. Children are not allowed with parents in this program.

The orphan court handles which types of cases?

Northampton County Court is a small division but handles many responsibilities that include adoption, trusts, estates of the deceased person, the appointment of guardians for minors and incapacitated persons, parental rights and marriage license termination. They also issue birth and death certified copies of records from the year 1893 to 1936. The orphan court hearing will be held on every Tuesday.

What happens in the cases of criminal matters?

Northampton County Court criminal court handles all crime-related matters that include murder, kidnapping etc. The magistrate district will handle the criminal matters, hears the preliminary hearing and decides the summary of crimes. Criminal cases involve the process of the pre-trial conference, criminal trial process, sentencing, and then the summary appeal and summary ARD.

What happens in the arraignments of criminal cases?

Northampton County Court arraignments are conducted by a member of the court. In this process, the defendant had to be present with a copy of the charges that are imposed on them. The attorney must also be presented on that day. This process allows certain defendants to take responsibility for their actions and receives positive consideration through the sentencing of the court. If the case is not solved then a trial will be held in the court and the person with all proof and the attorney must appear on time.

The juvenile court provides which types of services?

Northampton County juvenile court handles matters in which a minor age person is involved. The matters include cases in which a child is neglected or abused by their guardian and then the court will protect them. The court also handles cases in which the minor does a violation that is considered to be a crime if it is done by the adult.

What are the fine and court case costs for cases and matters?

Northampton County Court's fine and court cost depends upon the matters you are involved in. $38 is the cost for the order of execution, $17 for levy objection, $4.5 for appeal transcript or certiorari, $48.50 fine for all the summary convictions except for motor vehicles, $ 63 for felony cases and $55 for misdemeanor cases etc.

How can I apply for a marriage license?

Northampton County Court marriage license is given by the orphan court. You can apply for a license by visiting the orphan court division with your spouse and fill the application form. Those people that got married in Pennsylvania can apply for this application. The license is valid for up to three days.

FAQ:

What is the cost of the co-parenting education program?

$25 per participant is the cost of a co-parenting education program.

What is a language access plan?

The language access plan is provided by the Northampton County of Common Pleas. It is a facility that provides all court services and all cases proceeding to the deaf or any person who feels difficulty in hearing. In this way, they all can be part of all the cases proceeding and do not feel difficulty in any matter.

How can I request an interpreter?

You can request an interpreter by sending an email to the interpreter services at https://www.nccpa.org/emaildirect/Interpreter-Requests. You had to contact them as soon as possible otherwise they cannot provide you with an interpreter before the hearing.
